Finally, attention maps alone might highlight where the model is looking, but not why—for deeper insight, one might need to analyze the learned patch embeddings or incorporate textual concept explanations. To qualitatively compare the visual explanation performance of widely used XAI methods, we present saliency maps generated by Grad-CAM, RISE, and LIME on the same input image, as illustrated in Figure 11. These methods represent different categories of XAI techniques: Grad-CAM is a gradient-based attribution method, SmoothGrad adds noise for improved saliency visualization, and transformer-based XAI leverages self-attention mechanisms to capture global dependencies, aligning more naturally with clinical semantics [68,76]. This paper systematically examined explainable AI methods in computer vision, covering attribution-based techniques (Grad-CAM, SmoothGrad, DeConvNets, CAM, and their variants), perturbation-based approaches (with a focus on RISE), and emerging transformer-based explanation methods.

results.title: Comparative analysis of AI support levels in clinical ...
results.content: However, the specific requirements and preferences for AI explainability across different medical specialties remain largely unexplored, especially in trauma care settings where rapid and accurate interpretation of imaging studies by various specialists directly impacts patient outcomes32 in deep learning-based medical image analysis. While radiologists showed no significant additional time improvement between sessions 2 and 3, emergency physicians and trauma surgeons achieved further efficiency with AI-visual guidance, particularly in interpreting TN cases (Supplementary Table 1), reaching average interpretation times below 10 s per PXR. In this study, our findings demonstrate that AI assistance substantially improved trauma PXR interpretation across all specialties, with diagnostic accuracy increasing from 0.870 to 0.940 and interpretation time reducing by more than 50% (22.70–9.58 s). These comprehensive improvements in accuracy, efficiency, and confidence suggest that AI assistance could significantly enhance clinical workflow in trauma care settings, particularly benefiting non-radiologist physicians. In conclusion, our findings suggest that AI assistance improved interpretation performance in selected trauma imaging settings, particularly among non-radiologist physicians.

results.title: Evaluation of the impact of AI-driven personalized learning ...
results.content: The experimental group received a 12-week personalized learning intervention through the Coze platform, with specific measures including: Dynamic learning path optimization: Weekly adjustment of learning content difficulty and sequence based on diagnostic test results; Affective sensing support: Real-time identification of learning emotions through natural language processing (NLP) with triggered motivational feedback; Intelligent resource recommendation: Integration of a 2,800-case medical database utilizing BERT models to match personalized learning resources; Clinical simulation interaction: Embedded virtual case system providing real-time operational guidance. The core innovative contributions and explicit research objectives of this study include: (1) rigorously assessing the effectiveness of this theoretically integrated AI-PLP compared to traditional teaching methods in enhancing medical students’ post-learning knowledge acquisition using an RCT design; (2) thoroughly investigating its positive influence on learning satisfaction; (3) analyzing the correlation between self-directed learning behaviors and academic performance, preliminarily revealing potential mechanisms; (4) providing detailed and transparent descriptions of platform construction and methodology (including the rationale for selecting the Coze platform, robot function design, personalized strategy implementation, data collection tools, and randomization process) to enhance the study’s reproducibility and scientific rigor.
